title: Fall back to UPower when the sysfs battery rate is implausible
head: 183594b992ad
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A plausible signed discharge current hides a good battery rate
leads.consequence: On batteries exposing negative current_now (an explicitly supported sign in the power-supply ABI), -500000 microamps x 12000000 microvolts is -6 W: the 200 W absolute guard accepts it, overwrites UPower's positive 7.3 W, then the >0 gate hides rate entirely in both outputs. The power panel shows an empty Discharging value, and the battery notification shows just capacity. Preserve magnitude when accepting the signed measurement, or retain UPower's positive rate when the signed measurement is rejected. Related open PR #13009 explicitly normalizes negative readings; its signed-rate regression test cannot pass against this head.
leads.triage: already_in_opus; Opus N1; #13009 6W expectation verified by coordinator rg on sol/pr-13009.diff:223-226

leads.summary: Readable but empty/non-numeric sysfs nodes erase a valid UPower rate
leads.consequence: An empty or non-numeric current_now or power_now passes the readability check. awk converts it to zero, the <=200 guard overwrites UPower's valid value with 0, and the new >0 gate drops the rate key and notification wattage. A malformed power_now also prevents trying valid current_now plus voltage_now. A missing node correctly falls back, but a present unreadable or bad node does not. Open PR #12755 adds read-success and numeric checks to this same block; its tests requiring 7.3W for 'unknown' cannot pass with this head. If both implementations merge without reconciling the guards, the test conflict or behavior persists.
leads.triage: already_in_opus; Opus N2 read-fail/empty rows; non-numeric variant and #12755 7.3W expectation verified by rg on sol/pr-12755.diff:77-85; published as related-PR mention only

leads.summary: Missing rate value silently leaves a blank power-panel stat
leads.consequence: With energy-rate absent or 0 and no usable sysfs measurement, the script intentionally omits the rate key rather than showing 0W. The power panel still displays a labeled 'Discharging'/'Charging' row but its value is the empty string; it does not show the unknown-value placeholder used for charge cycles and time. Consider a placeholder such as '—' for the missing measurement, retaining the deliberate omission of an untrustworthy watt figure. The plain notification deliberately omits the watt segment, so it has no empty separator.
leads.triage: already_in_opus; Opus: empty panel value vs placeholder is cosmetic; not published as a finding

leads.summary: New shell assertion does not assert that the rate key is omitted
leads.consequence: The new test passes for a spurious 'rate	' key with no W suffix, although its described output contract is omission of the entire key. Tighten the assertion to fail whenever the parsed shell output contains '^rate	', regardless of the value.
leads.triage: already_in_opus; Opus N3 shell_rate_empty_value; published in optional test note

limits: No PR discussions, reviews or comments were read. Related open PRs were examined by file lists and source diffs only.

The isolated run covered signed, malformed, empty, missing, and zero sysfs inputs against a 7.3 W UPower stub in both output modes, not hardware, a Quickshell compositor, or every battery state. Child stdout/stderr/status are individually saved and gated; review.py verify passed.

This boundary hunt did not run the entire shipped battery suite or assess the main 200 W cutoff policy. A package recipe/PKGBUILD is not present in the pinned repository; the existing installation package lists require no entry for modifying this existing script.
Other open PRs sharing the battery script and panel were searched; no confirmed behavioral merge conflict beyond #12755 and #13009 was included as an issue.

flags.claim: The ACPI battery, ACPI SBS and Surface drivers report unsigned values
flags.why: True for ACPI SBS (abs(), sbs.c:193-200) and Surface (u32 present_rate, surface_battery.c:599-606). The ACPI battery driver applies no sign: it passes the firmware value through as rate_now*1000, with rate_now an int (battery.c:102, 250-256 at v7.2; 265-271 at v7.2.5). The value is positive on correct firmware but can be negative on buggy firmware, and #13108 itself is the ACPI driver reporting current_now=-65041000. The same compressed wording is in the bottom line of my final report (point 3). My N1 section carries the qualifier ('A negative ACPI value only comes from firmware bugs, like #13108 itself').

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up on [the earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13111#issuecomment-5825015978) and [the author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13111#issuecomment-5825678720), checked at `183594b9`.

**Verified:** both earlier findings and the earlier test note are resolved at this head.

| Earlier point | Result at `183594b9` |
|---|---|
| 4× ratio shows a stale UPower rate after load steps | **Resolved.** Only the 200 W cap remains. 60 W sysfs with UPower at 8 W now shows `60W`, and charging 65 W with UPower at 10 W shows `65W`. The new load-step case fails on `b7c9fae3` (`rate 8W`) and passes here. |
| Fallback can print `0W` | **Resolved.** With sysfs rejected and UPower at 0 or missing, the `rate` line and the plain-output wattage segment are omitted (`b7c9fae3` printed `0W`). The power panel replaces its battery data on each refresh and reads `rate \|\| ""`, so a missing key shows an empty value with no stale rate (checked in source, not run in the panel). The battery notification prints `… · 56Wh`. |
| Optional test improvement | **Resolved.** Removing the cap now fails the suite, and cases for UPower at 0, a load step and the `power_now` path were added. |

The #13108 values still give UPower's `7.5W` on both the `current_now × voltage_now` and `power_now` paths, and the existing 10.8 W case still passes.

### The new `> 0` check also hides plausible negative and zero sysfs readings

The cap compares the magnitude, so a plausible negative sysfs rate is accepted and replaces UPower's rate. The new `rate > 0` display check then drops it, so no rate is shown. The code comment describes a narrower case (sysfs rejected and UPower at 0 or none). Synthetic sysfs files and a stubbed `upower`:

```text
sysfs input                          UPower   base     b7c9fae3  183594b9
current_now -0.9 A × 12 V            10.5 W   -10.8W   -10.8W    (no rate)
power_now -10.8 W                    10.5 W   -10.8W   -10.8W    (no rate)
power_now read fails or is empty     5.5 W    0W       0W        (no rate)
```

**Impact:** the power-supply sysfs ABI says `current_now` is negative while discharging, and in-tree drivers such as bq27xxx, sbs-battery, max17042 and axp288 follow it. On those batteries the rate disappears while discharging even though UPower has a valid one. The ACPI battery driver applies no discharge sign (its values are positive unless the firmware is buggy, as in #13108), and ACPI SBS and Surface report unsigned values, so typical x86 laptops are not affected. How many Omarchy users run signed drivers is unknown. For the failed-read case from #12735 and #6895, which the description names as the same failure class, the symptom changes from `0W` to no rate, but UPower's valid rate is still discarded.

**Suggested change:** accept the sysfs rate only when `0 < |rate| <= 200` and store its magnitude, so other values fall back to UPower. That variant passes the current test unchanged and shows `10.8W` for the signed cases and UPower's `5.5W` for the failed read. The trade-off is that a genuine sysfs 0 (idle or full) would show UPower's possibly lagging rate. Open PR #13009 (same symptom on another MSI model) tests the signed case and expects the magnitude (`6W` for -0.5 A × 12 V). #12755 and #12649 target the failed-read case, and all three edit the same block.

**Optional test improvement:** the suite does not catch changing the check to `!= 0`, stripping the minus sign, or dropping the `-n $sysfs_rate` guard (which hides UPower's rate on a machine with no sysfs rate files). The omission check at test line 123 only looks for `W`, so an empty `rate` line would also pass. A signed-current case, a case with no sysfs rate files, and a check for any `^rate\t` line would pin these.

**Documentation note:** the PR description still describes the removed 4× ratio and 50 W floor.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** follow-up at `183594b9` against base and `b7c9fae3`: source review of the script, its test and consumers (power panel, battery notification), Linux v7.2 power-supply drivers and ABI, UPower 1.91.4, and where related open PRs edit the same script. The script and test ran in an isolated sandbox against synthetic sysfs files and a stubbed `upower`, including a scenario matrix, each new test case on each revision, and single-clause mutations of the new logic. No real hardware, UPower daemon or on-screen panel was tested.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
